sections.content:
24,675 people

were counted on the census as "barristers and judges" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Barristers and judges prepare and conduct court cases on behalf of clients, preside over judicial proceedings, and pronounce judgements within a variety of court settings and tribunals.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "barristers and judges", 13.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "barristers and judges" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "barristers and judges" included:

  • hotel and accommodation managers and proprietors
  • managers and proprietors in forestry, fishing and related services
  • professional/chartered company secretaries

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "barristers and judges" there were more men than women (55.2% compared with 44.8%).

This means "barristers and judges" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 55.2% and women made up 44.8% of "barristers and judges"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "barristers and judges" included:

  • restaurant and catering establishment managers and proprietors
  • publicans and managers of licensed premises
  • biological scientists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "barristers and judges" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "barristers and judges" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "barristers and judges", 10.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (81.5% compared with 18.5%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (59.4%) than an employee (40.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Camden, this is in the same region of London.
